nodes.label: FunkMaxExport v0.6.42 LGPMNM Wrench Vhot Static Proof
FreeAim Pose Overhaul v1.47 Test
nodes.rationale: Pose overhaul improved right-hand pose math but introduced a visible roll regression on both hands (rawRoll +53 published as clBank -53) and left snap-turn unproven because the capture had no turn proof lines.

nodes.label: Weapon Roll Inversion Regression (v1.47->v1.48)
nodes.rationale: v1.47's pose overhaul flipped the visible weapon roll sign for both hands; v1.48 fixed it by flipping the bank sign in the shared CameraLocalBankFromForwardUp helper and the Squirrel SS2VRPhysBankFromBasis helper. Fixing this did not solve the larger HMD-bleed problem.

nodes.label: v1.43/v1.44 Test: Inventory Restored, Weapon Translation Split, Glove Default Promoted
v1.37 Multi-Feature Test: Bracket Near-Fixed, Snap/Reload/Glove Good, Movement Dead
Gravity-Glove Yank Mechanism (HL:Alyx-style Pull)
nodes.rationale: Left grip selects/highlights an object; a backward yank of the hand velocity-servos it to the hand, then hands off to normal smoothed hold/release. Early implementation used a positive-only pull-speed threshold, which silently failed when the measured yank was signed negative for real hand motion (pullSpeed=-4.80).

nodes.label: Two-Hand Support Left-Hand Pitch Inversion
Native Left-Stick Movement Action Bridge
nodes.rationale: Publishes thumbstick state to a KEX config var consumed by Squirrel as held in-game actions; initial version was gated behind the legacy keyboard_emulation master, which was too strict and produced no in-game movement at all.

nodes.label: HMD-Authoritative Smooth-Turn Sign/Gain Calibration Saga
nodes.rationale: Multi-build saga to make player-capsule yaw track HMD-authoritative smooth-turn input: request-based yaw step ignored KEX's real accumulator gain (ratio ~-0.85); observed-KEX-yaw mode overcompensated due to prime/reset bugs; the eventual same-sign fix required separating snap vs smooth pixel-per-degree gain and a distinct kexMouseSign from userSign; final architecture used authViewSign plus display_baseline=smooth_authoritative_kex_delta_display_flip/same_sign to decouple body-turn sign from display-correction sign.

nodes.label: Selection Bracket Double-Vision / Depth Ghost
nodes.rationale: The VR selection bracket is a single world-locked OpenXR quad, so doubling/shimmering could only occur if it renders at the wrong depth while the eyes converge on the real object (distM jumping 2.8<->21m). Root cause is bad picking/depth placement, not a true stereo double-render.

nodes.label: Frob: Collision-less Wall-Fixture Selection Saga
nodes.rationale: Small wall fixtures (card slots, switches, keypads) have no own collision, so every ray-based pick passes through them; desktop SS2 instead selects by screen-space cursor proximity. Multiple misdiagnoses (vertical miscalibration, native-picker-calibration) were chased before the true root cause (head-local cursor vs KEX render-camera frame mismatch) was found, fixed via a camera-ray cursor, then finally solved architecturally via a Squirrel world-space semantic scan + engine-frob publish-back.

nodes.label: Frob Misdiagnosis: Vertical Cursor Miscalibration (SUPERSEDED)
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: detection correlated with injected cursor Y, so the fix was believed to be a static aim_flat_fov/offset_y calibration constant. Superseded once world_frob_prefer_native exposed that KEX's native cursor-pick just isn't precise enough for small VR targets, and later that the whole cursor was in the wrong reference frame.

nodes.label: Frob Misdiagnosis: world_frob_prefer_native Cursor-Projection Miscalibration (SUPERSEDED)
nodes.rationale: WRONG THEORY: believed the fix was to trust the raw segment-trace hit point (gated by frobbability) instead of KEX's imprecise screen-cursor pick. Superseded by discovering the true problem was that the frob cursor is projected in head-local space while the scene is rendered from the offset KEX camera -- a reference-frame mismatch, not a precision/gating problem.

nodes.label: Frob Root Cause: Head-Local Cursor vs KEX Render-Camera Frame Mismatch
nodes.rationale: TRUE ROOT CAUSE. The frob cursor is projected in HEAD-LOCAL space (invHead = conjugate(predicted head orientation)) but the scene is rendered from the KEX camera, which differs from the head by ~21 deg yaw and a pitch sign flip plus pitch_bias_degrees. Any flat calibration offset only worked at one head pose and drifted at others; the fix projects the controller's world-space ray through the same KEX render-camera basis already captured for the bracket.

nodes.label: Frob Fix: Camera-Ray Cursor (aim_camera_ray_cursor)
nodes.rationale: Reprojects the game-world hit point of the controller ray through the render-camera basis (not the head-local basis) to derive the screen cursor, making frob selection head-stable by construction.

nodes.label: pick_camera_probe: ~16% Residual Head-Coupling Bug
nodes.rationale: pick_camera_probe writes the controller world ray directly into the engine pick-camera, correctly avoiding the 2D-cursor problem, but with the controller physically still, ~16% of head yaw still leaked into the 'fixed' ray because reconstructing R = latestPickBasis*invHMD does not cleanly handle the KEX/OpenXR yaw mirror+offset (kexYaw = -headtrackYaw - 33.6 deg).

nodes.label: Squirrel World-Space Frob Scan + Engine-Frob Publish-Back -- CONFIRMED WORKING
nodes.rationale: Final architecture: Squirrel scans all objects scoring by perpendicular distance to the published controller world ray (head/camera-independent), filters by FrobInfo/semantic name hints, publishes the chosen target back via ss2vr_hl, and interact_squirrel_engine_frob writes it into objectUnderCursor/frobTarget so the engine's native USE frobs it with full Frobber context. Resolved the multi-week left-hand world-interaction blocker end-to-end, including the card reader's inventory-context requirement that a raw scripted SendMessage(FrobWorldEnd) could not satisfy.

nodes.label: ss2vr.ini Known-Keys Allowlist Silent-Rejection Bug
nodes.rationale: A second known-keys allowlist in Config.cpp (separate from the parser if/else chain) silently rejected new ini keys with 'Ignoring unknown ss2vr.ini key', voiding a whole test capture before anyone noticed. Lesson: any new ini key needs the parser branch, the allowlist entry, and the ini template edited together.

nodes.label: Hover-Candidate Bounding-Radius Size Cap + Filter Diagnostic
nodes.rationale: Discovered the native KEX frob picker scores hover candidates as distance-minus-bounding_radius with no upper bound, so large objects (doors/tables) always beat small interactables regardless of aim precision. world_candidate_max_radius rejects oversized candidates before the native scorer runs.

nodes.label: VR View Effects System (GPU Post-Process: crt/aberration/lens/sharpen/glitch/edge)
nodes.rationale: Final 'keeper set' of 6 GPU scene-sampling post-process effects, driven by a D3D11 fullscreen pass at the CopyIntoSwapchain seam, with a reverse Squirrel->DLL trigger channel via the KexSetConfigRaw config-setter hook (set ss2vr_fx <effect>). That same config-setter hook was later found to collide with the unrelated weapon-pose bridge's own config-setter call, silently disabling weapon tracking.

nodes.label: VR Effects CPU-Overlay FPS Tank (root cause)
nodes.rationale: Creative overlay effects dropped framerate to ~10fps. Root cause: CPU-side regeneration of a 512^2 RGBA texture with per-pixel sin/cos/pow/exp every 90ms on the submit thread while the GPU sat idle. Fixed by moving to a GPU D3D11 fullscreen post-process pass instead of a CPU-regenerated overlay texture.

nodes.label: Native Dark Stereo-Enable Byte Probe (Dead End)
nodes.rationale: Tested whether the old pre-AE Dark engine stereo_enable/mirror_mode bytes could activate native side-by-side rendering in AE's D3D11 path. Console command and direct byte write both succeeded (readback confirmed) but produced no visible stereo output. Falsified as an activation route; parked in favor of the existing alternate-eye pair-lock baseline.

nodes.label: Weapon Viewmodel HMD Positional Parallax (double-applied HMD translation)
nodes.rationale: Moving the HMD with the controller held still made the weapon model slide away, as if HMD movement were doubled. Root cause: the pose bridge publishes controller-relative-to-head offset, then RenderView's own HMD 6DOF translation is applied again on top. Fixed with model_pose_compensate_hmd, which adds the HMD positional delta back into the CameraObj pose so it cancels the double application; projectile world origin stays on the raw physical pose so Stage A aim is unaffected.

nodes.label: FunkMaxExport 3ds Max LGMD Tool Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Project-owned (non-GPL, built fresh rather than porting the Blender Dark exporter) 3ds Max <-> LGMD v4 bridge, built in tiers: exact no-edit round-trip, Funk Direct (topology-preserving vertex move), and Funk Mesh (vertex move + full-face deletion), enabling forearm removal from first-person weapon viewmodels while keeping AE's runtime PointRig/CameraObj animation working.

nodes.label: Funk Direct Baked-Import-Pose Bug
nodes.rationale: Funk Direct exported Max's displayed/world-space vertex positions for animated subobjects (the reload-hand and slide), baking the Max import pose into the LGMD file so the reload hand became permanently stuck onscreen. Fixed by choosing raw vs inverse-node-transform coordinates per subobject, compared against the original LGMD local vertices.

nodes.label: Funk Mesh Stale Header Face-Count Crash
nodes.rationale: Funk Mesh compacted the LGMD face chunk after face deletion but left the header's face-count field at offset 0x3C unchanged, so AE walked past the compacted chunk using the old count and crashed with an access violation. Fixed by updating both the face count (0x3C) and vertex count (0x3E) header fields whenever chunks are rebuilt.

nodes.label: Funk Mesh BSP Node-Offset Hang
nodes.rationale: After fixing the face-count crash, the same compacted export instead hung/froze AE with runaway render-record allocation. Root cause: face-chunk compaction changed BSP node record sizes, but only subobject node offsets were updated -- stale child-node offsets inside type-1 split and type-2 call node headers still pointed into the middle of the compacted stream, so AE's traversal generated millions of bogus render records.

nodes.label: FunkMesh modinfo.json Missing 'title' Key Crash
nodes.rationale: The repack step used the JSON key 'name' instead of AE's expected 'title' and omitted 'requirements':[]. AE is not defensive here: a missing title becomes a non-string JSON value and the mod-list UI crashes calling asCString() on it, before the already-fixed model even loads.

nodes.label: Right-Hand Aim Misdiagnosis: Sealed-Class Monkey-Patch of NDShootTriggerScript.OnCreate
nodes.rationale: WRONG APPROACH: direct assignment to NDShootTriggerScript.OnCreate is not legal in the AE Squirrel runtime/class context ('[SS2VR-AIM] projectile aim patch failed: trying to set class'). The failure was mistaken at first for a DLL pose-bridge or native-fire problem; the actual fix required a supported hook route (a parallel SqRootScript attached via the same ND.Archetype helper Nightdive itself uses).

nodes.label: Right-Hand Aim Deferred-Timer Redirect Fix (v1.8, CONFIRMED)
nodes.rationale: The engine assigns a fired projectile's real launch velocity AFTER the script's OnCreate callback runs, so an immediate redirect always saw oldSpeed=0 and silently did nothing. Fix: re-apply the redirect from a SetOneShotTimer('SS2VRReaim', ...) deferred callback, which sees the real engine-assigned velocity (oldSpeed=300) and overwrites it along the controller ray while preserving speed.

nodes.label: Mod Load-Order/Priority Regression (KPF present but Squirrel not loaded)
nodes.rationale: Recurring failure mode: a KPF can appear in DarkDBMod's search paths and still fail to provide the active Squirrel load order if a higher-priority mod (e.g. sshock2ee) ships its own squirrel.ini first. The DLL side (pose bridge, native fire) can look fully alive while the Squirrel handler simply never loaded, producing a misleading 'regression' that looks like a code bug.

nodes.label: KPF Archive Backslash-Path Packaging Bug
nodes.rationale: A repack step wrote archive entries with backslash paths (sq_scripts\squirrel.ini) instead of forward slashes, which likely prevented AE from recognizing/running the Squirrel load order even though the KPF was present in the mod search path -- another silent-looking Squirrel-not-loaded failure mode distinct from priority ordering.

nodes.label: Save Patcher Default Insertion-Position Bug (first vs last)
nodes.rationale: The save patcher's add command defaulted to inserting the SS2VR mod entry FIRST in the saved game's mod table, which is the opposite of the desired effective load order (SS2VR needs to load after sshock2ee to win priority). Fixed by flipping the default --position to last.

nodes.label: Save Patcher Short-Root Save Shape Fix
nodes.rationale: A different/smaller save (smaller header_size/root object length/vtable length) failed the patcher's root-object shape guard even though the needed title/level/mods fields still parsed cleanly. Guard relaxed to accept shorter root objects as long as the specific required fields fit inside them.

nodes.label: FlatAim Native-Picker Diagonal Selection Offset
nodes.rationale: Even after 1:1-pixel visible-reticle-to-injected-picker logging proved no X/Y sign or overlay-placement error, the native KEX picker only selected objects when the visible reticle was aimed diagonally down-left of them. The user explicitly recognized this as the same shape as the VR mod's earlier frob 'offset diagonally'/tiny-sweet-spot problem; flat-pixel offset tuning was abandoned in favor of porting the SS2VR semantic world-space object scan + publish-back architecture to FlatAim.

nodes.label: FlatAim Save-Load Access-Violation Crash (near native hover-candidate scorer)
nodes.rationale: Recurring access violation (0xc0000005) on loading/reloading a save while FlatAim was active, backtrace repeatedly landing near the hooked native hover-candidate scorer (0x1404B9EB6 / static RVA 0x8D4700-0x8D4748). Successive hypotheses (per-frame ss2fa_hl config mutation, missing Squirrel heartbeat, the installed KexSetConfigRaw hook itself) were each ruled out in turn -- disabling the config hook entirely (configHook=0 configInstalled=0) still did not stop the crash, leaving the true cause unresolved at the end of this range.

nodes.label: Additive Left-Hand Viewmodel Spike (Phase 4.7)
nodes.rationale: Proof-of-concept second first-person viewmodel object cloned from the active weapon model, driven through the same Squirrel CameraObj property path proven by the right-hand handoff. Not true left-controller tracking yet: it follows the right hand's camera-local ss2vr_aim pose plus an offset because the left hand only publishes a world-space ss2vr_sel ray, not a camera-local pose.

nodes.label: Weapon Pose Bridge Disabled by Own Config-Setter Hook Collision
nodes.rationale: User reported losing motion-controller weapon tracking after enabling an offhand-animation probe; root cause was unrelated and self-inflicted: the VR view-effects/config-trigger MinHook had detoured the same KEX config-setter function the weapon pose bridge used to publish ss2vr_aim, so the bridge's own prologue-mismatch safety check saw its own patched bytes and refused to publish. Fixed by routing through the g_realSetConfigRaw trampoline when the hook is installed.

nodes.label: Weapon Model Rotational HMD Parallax (yaw/pitch/roll coupling)
nodes.rationale: After positional HMD-parallax compensation was fixed, a distinct rotational symptom remained: HMD yaw moves the pistol opposite, HMD pitch-down pushes the gun forward (and vice versa), and HMD roll rolls the pistol opposite. Addressed with a CameraObj-only rotational HMD compensation term layered after the existing positional compensation, plus a short pose latch/smoothing window; still jittery/unresolved at the end of this range.

nodes.label: Enemy Health Bar Misdiagnosis Correction: It Is Native
nodes.rationale: WRONG ASSUMPTION corrected: the team initially treated the enemy/target health bar as a build-from-scratch VR feature. A user screenshot proved AE already renders a native segmented HP bar in the flat 2D HUD layer. The real problem is VR placement/floating it above the world-space bracket, not implementing HP display from scratch.

nodes.label: Native UI Draw-Range Index Slice Map (Phase 2.8)
nodes.rationale: Percentage-based and index-range captures of the native D3D11 UI draw calls, isolating which draw-index bands correspond to which coherent inventory/HUD element clusters (ammo/toggles, research/map buttons, inventory panel, weapon icons, MFD/keycard buttons, etc.), intended to replace percentage-slice UI panel placement with real draw-identity-based floating panels.

nodes.label: Curved HUD/Inventory Panel Prototype
nodes.rationale: Cylindrical curvature applied to the floating inventory/HUD panel; low curvature felt small/far, high curvature (panel_curvature=0.95) felt close but the size-vs-distance scaling relationship still felt wrong, and curved mode disabled flat motion-controller inventory interaction as an expected side effect.
